reviewed_by: Claude: Butler supervisor powers behind an operator kill switch
reason: Adds Butler nebula.supervisor.* capabilities (audited shell/SSH, signals, runner control, repository publish, committed gate runs, cross-goal repo forensics, independent closure review on a different model, deterministic goal hygiene) behind NEBULA_BUTLER_SUPERVISOR_ENABLED, plus a no-self-approval gate in ControlAssistantWork.goal_action and claude-opus-5-5 limits. Python selects the three new suites (guardrails, audit, kill switch, real subprocess host tools, forensics on temp git repos, review gate and verdict application, hygiene against ChatGoalService/WorkService and real create_app ControlAssistantWork), the existing goal_action/goal-chat suites that exercise the edited goal_action path, test_context for model limits, and product-help discovery of the new settings-assistant row with the index digest.
exclusions: tests/v3/test_butler_capabilities.py and tests/v3/test_butler_recovery.py exercise the edited gateway and recovery hook and were run locally (only failures: test_scheduled_butler_can_edit_all_assistant_settings and test_act_switches_worker_to_provider_and_queues_only_the_parent, both failing identically on unmodified origin/main 6f6bb821); they are not selected so CI does not fail on those pre-existing defects. No UI, frontend, native or Playwright change: the feature is configured by Core service environment variables and reached through Butler's existing gateway. Local runs used Python 3.11.7. No full-suite approval.
